e-7163.knowledge_point: Finding the Complement of a Set Using a Venn Diagram
e-7163.problem:
Let $U = \{ a, b, c, d, e, f, g \}$ be the universal set and let $B = \{ b, d, f \}.$ What is $\overline{B}?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071504/assets/25f40492b0466495519d6ff94859d0cef4c206e291d31eba2a980732b497af31.png)
e-7163.worked_solution:
The complement of $B,$ denoted $\overline B,$ consists of all the elements in $U$ that are not in $B.$ To represent $\overline B,$ we will shade in all the area of $U$ that is *outside* of $B,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071504/assets/daad235ef63e127e99bf3eec7b7bbe75fe6adb969f5b54ebb5a3fb010773b680.png)

The elements in the shaded area are $a,$ $c,$ $e,$ and $g.$ These are the elements of $U$ that are not in $B.$ Therefore, the complement of $B$ is

$$
\overline{B} = \{ a,c,e,g \}.
$$

e-7164.knowledge_point: Finding the Complement of a Set Without a Venn Diagram
e-7164.problem: Let $U = \{ a, b, c, d, e, f, g \}$ be the universal set and let $A = \{ b, c, d, f, g \}.$ What is $\overline{A}?$
e-7164.worked_solution:
The complement of $A,$ denoted $\overline{A},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $A.$

The only elements of $U$ that are not in $A$ are $a$ and $e.$

Therefore, the complement of $A$ is

$$
\overline{A} = \{ a, e \}.
$$

e-7165.knowledge_point: Finding the Complement of a Set Given Using Ellipsis Notation
e-7165.problem: Let $U = \{ 1, 2, 3, \ldots, 30 \}$ be the universal set and let $B = \{ 5, 6, 7, \ldots, 28 \}.$ What is $\overline{B}?$
e-7165.worked_solution:
The complement of $B,$ denoted $\overline{B},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $B.$

The universal set $U$ consists of the integers $1$ through $30,$ while the set $B$ consists of the integers $5$ through $28.$

So, the only elements of $U$ that are not in $B$ are $1,$ $2,$ $3,$ $4,$ $29,$ and $30.$

Therefore, the complement of $B$ is

$$
\overline{B} = \{ 1,2,3,4,29,30 \}.
$$

Let $U={1,2,3,4,a,b,c}$ be the universal set and let $V={1,b}.$ What is $\overset{―}{V}?$
after.worked_solution:
The complement of $V,$ denoted $\overset{―}{V},$ consists of all the elements in $U$ that are not in $V.$ To represent $\overset{―}{V},$ we will shade in all the area of $U$ that is *outside* of $V,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071504/assets/5997d1aa469784f2bdddf0f90c6ca7f8c9dc0ff83886be35b28306ac1246a08b.png)

The elements in the shaded area are $2,3,4,a,$ and $c.$ These are the elements of $U$ that are not in $V.$ Therefore, the complement of $V$ is

$$
\overset{―}{V}={2,3,4,a,c}.
$$

Let $U={1,2,3,a,b,c,d}$ be the universal set and let $W={3,b,c}.$ What is $\overset{―}{W}?$
after.worked_solution:
The complement of $W,$ denoted $\overset{―}{W},$ consists of all the elements in $U$ that are not in $W.$ To represent $\overset{―}{W},$ we will shade in all the area of $U$ that is *outside* of $W,$ as follows:

$$
\overset{―}{W}={1,2,a,d}.
$$

EXPLANATION

The complement of W, denoted W―, consists of all the elements in U that are not in W. To represent W―, we will shade in all the area of U that is outside of W, as follows:

Let $U={1,2,3,a,b,c,d}$ be the universal set and let $W={3,b,c}.$ What is $\overset{―}{W}?$
content.worked_solution:
The complement of $W,$ denoted $\overset{―}{W},$ consists of all the elements in $U$ that are not in $W.$ To represent $\overset{―}{W},$ we will shade in all the area of $U$ that is *outside* of $W,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071504/assets/365a6446a4ec6993447cf11190c8311027fac5bc9b0b36e85a4452fdfe85f7fa.png)

The elements in the shaded area are $1,2,a,$ and $d.$ These are the elements of $U$ that are not in $W.$ Therefore, the complement of $W$ is

$$
\overset{―}{W}={1,2,a,d}.
$$

after.worked_solution:
The complement of $X,$ denoted $\overset{―}{X},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $X.$

$$

a
{1,3,6,9}
b
{1,3,5,7,9}
c
{3,5,7,9}
d
{0,3,6,9}
e

decision.explanation: Removing the elements of A (2, 4, 6, 8, and 10) from U leaves {1,3,5,7,9}.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: If $U={1,2,3,…,10}$ is the universal set and $A={2,4,6,8,10},$ then the complement of $A$ is
after.worked_solution:
The complement of $A,$ denoted $\overset{―}{A},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $A.$

The elements of $U$ that are not in $A$ are $1,$ $3,$ $5,$ $7,$ and $9.$

Therefore, the complement of $A$ is

$$
\overset{―}{A}={1,3,5,7,9}.
$$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem: If $U={p,q,r,s,t,u}$ is the universal set and $S={q,s,t},$ then the complement of $S$ is
after.worked_solution:
The complement of $S,$ denoted $\overset{―}{S},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $S.$

The only elements of $U$ that are not in $S$ are $p,$ $r,$ and $u.$

Therefore, the complement of $S$ is

$$
\overset{―}{S}={p,r,u}.
$$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem: If $U={2,4,6,8,…,20}$ is the universal set and $B={4,8,12,16,20},$ then the complement of $B$ is
after.worked_solution:
The complement of $B,$ denoted $\overset{―}{B},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $B.$

The elements of $U$ that are not in $B$ are $2,$ $6,$ $10,$ $14,$ and $18.$

Therefore, the complement of $B$ is

$$
\overset{―}{B}={2,6,10,14,18}.
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: If $U={a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h}$ is the universal set and $D={a,d,g}$ then the complement of $D$ is
after.worked_solution:
The complement of $D,$ denoted $\overset{―}{D},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $D.$

$$
\overset{―}{D}={b,c,e,f,h}.
$$

after.problem: If $U={-20,-19,-18,…,20}$ is the universal set and $A={1,2,3,…,20},$ then $\overset{―}{A}=$
after.worked_solution:
The complement of $A,$ denoted $\overset{―}{A},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $A.$

The universal set $U$ consists of the integers $-20$ through $20,$ while he set $A$ consists of the integers $1$ through $28.$

So, the only elements of $U$ that are not in $A$ are the integers $-20$ through $0.$

$$
\overset{―}{A}={-20,-19,-18,…,0}.
$$

Question 12

If U={−20,−18,−16,−14,…,20} is the universal set and A={−20,−16,−12,−8,…,20}, then A―=

a
{−16,−14,−12,−10,…,16}
b
{−18,−14,−10,−6,−2,2,6,10,14,18}
c
{−18,−12,−6,0,6,12,18}

{−18,−16,−14,−12,…,18}
e
{−20,−16,−12,−8,−4,0,4,8,12,16}
Submit

decision.explanation: U contains all even integers from -20 through 20. A contains the multiples of 4 in that range. Removing them leaves {-18,-14,-10,-6,-2,2,6,10,14,18}.

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
The complement of $A,$ denoted $\overset{―}{A},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $A.$

The universal set $U$ consists of the even integers $-20$ through $20,$ while the set $A$ consists of the multiples of $4$ from $-20$ through $20.$

So, the only elements of $U$ that are not in $A$ are the even integers from $-18$ through $18$ that are not multiples of $4.$

Therefore, the complement of $A$ is

$$
\overset{―}{A}={-18,-14,-10,-6,-2,2,6,10,14,18}.
$$

Question 12
?

If U={−20,−18,−16,−14,…,20} is the universal set and A={−20,−16,−12,−8,…,20}, then A―=

a
{−16,−14,−12,−10,…,16}
b
{−18,−14,−10,−6,−2,2,6,10,14,18}
c
{−18,−12,−6,0,6,12,18}
d
{−18,−16,−14,−12,…,18}
e
{−20,−16,−12,−8,−4,0,4,8,12,16}
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The complement of A, denoted A―, consists of every element in the universal set U that is not in the set A.

The universal set U consists of the even integers −20 through 20, while the set A consists of the multiples of 4 from −20 through 20.

So, the only elements of U that are not in A are the even integers from −18 through 18 that are not multiples of 4.

Therefore, the complement of A is

A―={−18,−14,−10,−6,−2,2,6,10,14,18}.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem: Let $U={a,b,c,…,z}$ be the universal set and $Y={a,b,c,…,j}$, then $\overset{―}{Y}=$
after.worked_solution:
The complement of $Y,$ denoted $\overset{―}{Y},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $Y.$

The universal set $U$ consists of the letters $a$ through $z,$ while the set $Y$ consists of the letters $a$ through $j.$

So, the only elements of $U$ that are not in $Y$ are the letters $k$ through $z.$

Therefore, the complement of $Y$ is

$$
\overset{―}{Y}={k,l,m,…,z}.
$$

after.name: Question 15
after.problem: If $U={5,10,15,…,50}$ is the universal set and $C={5,15,25,35,45},$ then the complement of $C$ is
after.worked_solution:
The complement of $C,$ denoted $\overset{―}{C},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $C.$

The elements of $U$ that are not in $C$ are $10,20,30,40,$ and $50.$

Therefore, the complement of $C$ is

$$
\overset{―}{C}={10,20,30,40,50}.
$$
